A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DyWA, with matching tasks, methods, and main experiments. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. V1 ends after its references; v2 supplies supplementary material that v1 mentions but does not include.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulation benchmarks, component ablations, and physical-robot experiments in Tables 1–4, including 34 successful real-world trials out of 50.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and additionally reports teacher-policy and conditioning comparisons in supplementary Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: The teacher–student pipeline, joint action/state prediction, history-based dynamics adaptation, FiLM conditioning, and variable-impedance control remain unchanged. V2 clarifies the world-action-model definition and loss notation and supplies architectural details; these do not establish a changed proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use 323 training objects, 10 unseen simulation objects at five scales, the same three perception tracks, 10 real-world objects, surface-friction tests, and manipulation applications. The supplementary asset galleries and simulation examples document retained coverage rather than establish new tasks or populations.

E2.justification: Table 1 now includes HACMan in the reported unknown-state comparisons with three and one camera views, where v1 showed dashes. Supplementary Table 6 also explicitly compares cross-attention conditioning against MLP and FiLM. The other benchmark comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The retained experiments preserve the perception tracks, 200K teacher and 500K student training iterations, success thresholds, and real-world ICP assessment. Supplementary pose-generation and hyperparameter specifications disclose previously omitted settings without establishing altered protocols. The additional ablations use the retained task and success-rate metric.

E4.justification: V2 supplies the previously referenced but absent teacher-policy and conditioning analyses. Tables 5–6 test adding world modeling/FiLM to the teacher and replacing student FiLM with cross-attention. Figure 12 adds qualitative simulation trajectories. The existing component ablations, loss curves, and friction-robustness study remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. V2's Table 3 caption explains the five attempts per object already explicit in v1's fractions; it does not introduce additional repetitions or a new reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 fills HACMan's unknown-state entries with 3.0(23.6)/4.1(26.5) for three views and 1.5(17.9)/2.9(18.3) for one view, ordered seen/unseen; parentheses report planar-task rates. Table 5 adds teacher results of 94.1, 93.9, and 93.5, while Table 6 adds cross-attention's 70.1. Its MLP/FiLM results repeat existing values. Main DyWA results remain unchanged, and Figure 12 adds qualitative simulation outcomes.

T1.justification: Supplementary Section 7.1 adds explicit mathematical definitions of the teacher reward, reaching/contact potentials, and energy penalty in Equations 8–13. These formalize the previously referenced reward design. No theorem or proof is added; the main loss-equation edits primarily clarify notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: joint action/state learning with dynamics adaptation, single-view manipulation without pose tracking, generalization across physical conditions, and a simulation benchmark. The headline performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 explains that benefits primarily concern student distillation, attributing the teacher's nearly unchanged performance to saturation. It hypothesizes distribution-shift sensitivity for cross-attention. Section 4.2 replaces 'action coverage' with 'action loss convergence' and 'indivisibility' with 'complementarity.' The stated limitations concerning symmetric, transparent, and specular objects remain.

D1.justification: The supplement substantially expands reproducibility information: segmentation, reward construction, stable-pose sampling, PointNet++ grouping, history length, layer dimensions, optimizer settings, and parallel-environment counts are now documented in Sections 6–11 and Tables 7–10. These are disclosures rather than demonstrated implementation changes. One discrepancy remains: Table 8 lists a three-output rotation predictor despite Section 3.3 specifying a 9D rotation representation.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 changes the relationship to JOWA from explicit similarity to a distinction between model classes and adds joint observation/action prediction literature, including Prediction with Action and Unified World Models. Some earlier visual-foresight and Dreamer discussion is removed. DAgger, reward-shaping, and appearance-related references are added, while the broader manipulation positioning remains.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained. V2 condenses the world-model related work, adds a definition paragraph, refines terminology and application descriptions, corrects wording, expands affiliations, and adds acknowledgements. Supplementary Sections 6–11 organize the newly supplied material without substantially restructuring the main narrative.

P2.justification: V2 substantially extends visual documentation through robot/camera setup illustrations, object-asset galleries, and simulation trajectories in Figures 7–12, plus ablation and implementation Tables 5–10. Existing figures and table structures are largely preserved, with localized illustration, spacing, and caption edits, including clarification of Table 3's trial counts.

improvement.justification: V2 improves auditability by supplying implementation information missing from v1's referenced supplement and exposing omitted HACMan comparisons and targeted ablation results. These additions support the existing conclusions more transparently. However, uncertainty reporting remains absent, and the new Table 8 introduces an unresolved rotation-output discrepancy with Section 3.3. The net gain is useful completeness and reproducibility support, with remaining limits to its reliability.
